Definition: from G4111; spread out "flat" ("plot"), i.e. broad:--wide.
BiblicalUsage: Platys means wide, broad — and in the New Testament it stands in the plural for the streets, the wide open places of a town. Hypocrites love to pray standing in the corners of the streets in Matthew 6:5, and the crowds will say they ate and drank in His presence and He taught in their streets in Luke 13:26. But of the Servant, Matthew 12:19 says neither shall any man hear His voice in the streets.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the streets hear two kinds of noise — men praying to be seen, and the Servant who will not raise His voice. I hold that His quietness is the louder witness.
